claim: A public employee who is demoted within weeks of testifying before a legislative committee on matters of public concern presents sufficient temporal proximity to survive summary judgment on a First Amendment retaliation claim. The court held that protected speech need not be the sole motivating factor, only a substantial one, in the adverse employment decision.
citation: Pellegrino v. Cuyahoga County Board of Elections, 78 F.3d 541 (6th Cir. 1996)
initial_reasoning: In Pellegrino v. Cuyahoga County Board of Elections, the Sixth Circuit held that a public employee’s demotion or dismissal within a short period after testifying before a legislative committee on matters of public concern can survive summary judgment if the adverse action was substantially motivated by the protected speech, even if other factors also contributed. The court emphasized that the protected conduct need not be the sole motivating factor, only a substantial one.
